newsitem.title: JAPAN: Drunken passenger briefly hijacks Japan airliner.
newsitem.headline: Drunken passenger briefly hijacks Japan airliner.

text.p: A drunken passenger wielding a fruit knife briefly hijacked an All Nippon Airways (ANA) airliner on a domestic flight on Monday before being overpowered by the crew, a Transport Ministry spokesman said.

The spokesman told Reuters the passenger jumped from his seat about 10 minutes before the aircraft landed in the southern city of Fukuoka at the end of a one-hour scheduled flight from Itami Airport on the border of Osaka and Hyogo prefectures.
He then burst into the cockpit with a fruit knife and demanded that when the aircraft landed at Fukuoka it should be refuelled and take off again for an unnamed international airport.
The Boeing 777 was carrying 182 passengers and 10 crew.
The hijacker, a Japanese man in his thirties identified by the ministry as Yuichi Yano, was overpowered by the crew after leaving the aircraft at Fukuoka. No one was hurt in the brief drama.
"The pilot advised there was a hijacking but no one was injured in the incident and the ANA crew overpowered the man, who was drunk," the spokesman said.

The passengers, who were unaware there was a hijacking in progress, filed off the plane as normal after the hijacker said they could leave the aircraft. When the plane was empty the hijacker also started to walk down the stairs of the aircraft to the ground, the spokesman said.
Crew members jumped on him as he was leaving the aircraft and held him until police took him into custody.
All Nippon Airways Co Ltd is Japan's second-largest airline.
